POLICE HEADQUARTERS, 
HONG KONG. 


29th December, 1936. 


Sir, 

I have the honour to request your assistance 
in trecing Mr. Robert George WITCHELL, a British subject, 
sO years of Sietig whe is employed aes a clerk in the 
Passport Cffice of this department. He left Hong Kong 
for Shanghei on the 25th November, 1936, in the S.S. 
"Empress of Asia" having been granted 12 days' casual 
leave. He has not yet returned to duty, snd although 
he has already long over-stayed his leave I have re- 
ceived no word of explanation from him. 

I understand thet Nr. Witchell's wife, Mrs. 
M.K. Witchell, is living in Shanghai at No. 577 du 
Rol Albert, Appartment 5. It is possible that she 
may be able to give some information concerning her 
husband elthough I understand that they have recently 
not been on best of terms. 

I shall be very grateful for any assistance 
you can give me in this matter. 

I have the honour to be, 4 
Sir, 


Your obedient servant, 


Act. Commissioner of Police. 


The Commissioner of Police, 
Shanghai Municipal Council,

POLICE HEADQUARTERS,
HONG KONG.
27th. January 1939.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of your letter
No.S.B. D8950 (C.) dated January the 13th.1939, and to inform
you that we are in receipt of the following information
concerning Mr.Robert George Witchell.

Mr.Witchell left Hong Kong per S.S."Empress of Asia" on
25.II.38, booked to Shanghai. He was accompanied by Mrs.
Ursula Lloyd, a British Subject, with whom Witchell appears
to have been on rather intimate terms. Mrs.Lloyd was booked
through to Yokohama, and it appears that Witchell also
continued the journey to Yokohama with her. Confirmation has
been received here that both Witchell and Mrs.Lloyd sailed
from Yokohama for Honolulu on 8.12.38. per S.S."Chichibu Maru".

It is also known that Witchell is in possession of a
valid British Passport and that he obtained a temporary
visitor's visa for the U.S.A. on 25.II.38,the date of sailing.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
p.Commissioner of Police.

The Commissioner of Police,

Shanghai.

香港警察总局，
1939年1月27日。

先生：

谨此确认收到阁下1939年1月13日来函，编号S.B. D8950 (C.)，并告知我方已收到关于罗伯特·乔治·威切尔（Robert George Witchell）先生的如下信息。

威切尔先生于38年2月25日乘坐“亚细亚皇后”号轮船离开香港，预订目的地为上海。同行者为乌苏拉·劳埃德（Ursula Lloyd）女士，系英国臣民，威切尔与其关系似乎相当亲密。劳埃德女士的船票直达横滨，看来威切尔也随她继续前往横滨。此处已收到确认，威切尔和劳埃德女士均于38年12月8日乘坐“秩父丸”号轮船从横滨启航前往火奴鲁鲁。

另悉，威切尔持有有效的英国护照，并于38年2月25日（即启航当日）获得了美国临时访客签证。

谨此奉复，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
代理警务总监。

致：
警务总监，

上海。

WRS: FIT

Subject Letter from Hongkong Police enquiring whereabouts of Robert
George Mitchell, 30, British.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. J. S.

With reference to Special Branch report on the
subject of above, a coded telegram was received from
the Hongkong Police at 5 p.m. 14/1/39, which was decoded
by Mr. Ford, Vice Consul, H.B.M. Consulate-General, and
reads as follows:-
"With reference to my letter of December 29th
and my telegram of January 11th Mitchell known to have left
Shanghai for Yokohama and Kobe
C.I.D. Police"
Continued enquiries have up to date failed to
ascertain the name of the ship on which Mitchell left
Shanghai.

Logan
D. S. I.

Seen by. D. S. B.
P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)
D.C. (Special Branch).

CONFIDENTIAL
S.1, Special Branch,
January 12, 1939.

Letter from Hongkong Police enquiring whereabouts of
Robert George Witchell, 30, British.
------------------

With reference to the attached letter, dated December 29,
1938, from the Acting Commissioner of Police, Hongkong, to the
Commissioner of Police, Shanghai, enquiring the whereabouts of
one Robert George Witchell, age 30, British, employed as a
clerk in the Passport Office, Hongkong, who left Hongkong for
Shanghai on November 25, 1938 in the s.s. "Empress of Asia"
having been granted 12 days' casual leave, enquiries confirmed
that Witchell arrived in Shanghai on November 27, 1938, having
travelled from Hongkong first class in the s.s. "Empress of
Asia". It was learned from the local office of the Canadian
Pacific Steamship Co. that Witchell gave as his address, 392
Route Ferguson, Flat 4 (Tel.75836), which is the residence of
his aunt. This lady upon being interviewed, stated that she
had received a letter from Witchell's mother in Hongkong asking
for information concerning his whereabouts but denied having
seen or heard anything of him in Shanghai. She stated that she
had reason to believe that he would avoid meeting her as she
was usually severe with him on account of his escapades with
women. She made the request that her name should not be men-
tioned in any report as she did not wish to be associated with
her nephew in any way, especially as her husband is employed as
a teacher in the S.M.C. Education Department.

Witchell's wife (registered at H.B.M. Consulate-General)
who resides at Apt. 5, 377 Avenue du Roi Albert, when interview-
ed expressed surprise upon learning that her husband had come
to Shanghai and stated that she was unable to give any informa-
tion that would assist in tracing his whereabouts. She stated
that she was living apart from him in consequence of his habit
of consorting with other women. She was aware that he was
heavily in debt in Hongkong, but had regularly received her
monthly allowance of HK.$180.00 per month up to the end of

1939年1月12日。

香港警方来函查询英国人罗伯特·乔治·威切尔，30岁之下落。
------------------

参照附件中1938年12月29日香港代理警务总监致上海警务总监的来信，查询罗伯特·乔治·威切尔（Robert George Witchell），30岁，英国人，香港护照办事处职员之下落。该员于1938年11月25日获准12天临时休假，乘坐“亚细亚皇后”号轮船离开香港前往上海。经调查证实，威切尔于1938年11月27日抵达上海，乘坐“亚细亚皇后”号轮船从香港头等舱前来。从加拿大太平洋轮船公司本地办事处获悉，威切尔提供的地址为费格生路392号4室（电话75836），这是其姑母的住所。在接受问询时，这位女士表示曾收到威切尔母亲从香港寄来的信件，询问其下落，但否认在上海见过或听说过他的任何消息。她表示有理由相信他会避免与她见面，因为她通常对他与女性的风流韵事管教严厉。她请求在任何报告中不要提及她的姓名，因为她不希望以任何方式与侄子产生关联，尤其是因为她的丈夫在工部局教育处担任教师。

威切尔的妻子（在英国驻沪总领事馆注册）居住在阿尔伯特王路377号5室，在接受问询时，得知丈夫来到上海表示惊讶，并称无法提供任何有助于追踪其下落的信息。她表示，由于他有与其他女性交往的习惯，她已与他分居。她知道他在香港负债累累，但直到月底一直定期收到每月180.00港元的生活费。

allowances have not been received. In this connection it is
noteworthy that on November 23, 1938, Mrs. Witchell addressed
an urgent telegram to her husband threatening to take legal
proceedings against him should he fail to remit the overdue
allowances. As he left Hongkong on November 25, 1938 it would
appear that his departure may have had some connection with the
receipt of the telegram mentioned. Besides the telegram, Mrs.
Witchell addressed several pressing letters to her husband
which, combined with the telegram and alleged debts, may have
made him decide to abscond.

At 4.30 p.m. January 11, 1939, a coded telegram was
received from the Hongkong Police, which was decoded by Mr.
W.J. McLaughlin, Vice-Consul, H.B.M. Consulate-General, stating
that Witchell is suspected of having misappropriated a number of
blank Hongkong passports from stock.

It is reasonable to suppose therefore that Witchell contem-
plated absconding and, having access to the Hongkong blank pass-
ports would have experienced little difficulty in forging one
or more, doubtless under an assumed name or names.

A photograph of Witchell was obtained from his wife and
several copies made. These have been shown to the various hotel
and boarding house managers as well as to shipping agents but up
to date no useful information concerning Witchell has been
obtained. Examination of the various shipping lists show that
Witchell has not left Shanghai by ship under his own name but it
is quite possible that he may have departed under an assumed
name and using one of the misappropriated passports which, with
his special knowledge acquired in course of his employment as
passport clerk, he could with little difficulty forge.
Enquiries have been made at the various Consulates in Shanghai
but the officials were unable to identify the photograph of
Witchell. It is likely that if he applied for a visa to enter a

1938年10月。1938年11月、12月及1939年1月的生活费尚未收到。在此方面，值得注意的是，1938年11月23日，威切尔夫人的确向丈夫发出了一封紧急电报，威胁若他不汇出逾期生活费，将对他采取法律行动。鉴于他于1938年11月25日离开香港，看来他的离港可能与收到上述电报有关。除了电报外，威切尔夫人的确还向丈夫发出了几封措辞强硬的信件，结合电报和所谓的债务，可能促使他决定潜逃。

1939年1月11日下午4时30分，收到香港警方发来的密码电报，由英国驻沪总领事馆副领事W.J. McLaughlin先生解码，称威切尔涉嫌从库存中盗用多份空白香港护照。

因此，有理由推测威切尔预谋潜逃，且由于他能接触到香港的空白护照，伪造一份或多份护照对他来说并无太大困难，无疑会使用假名。

已从威切尔妻子处获得威切尔的照片并制作了几份副本。这些照片已出示给各家旅馆和寄宿公寓经理以及航运代理商，但截至目前未获得关于威切尔的任何有用信息。查阅各类船运名单显示，威切尔并未以本人名义乘船离开上海，但他完全可能使用假名并利用其中一份被盗用的护照离境，凭借其在护照职员任职期间获得的专门知识，他可以毫不费力地伪造护照。已向上海各领事馆进行查询，但官员们无法辨认威切尔的照片。如果他申请进入某国的签证，很可能……

to accept money from women and quoted an instance where he had
accepted money from a woman believed to be the neice of a Swiss
Consul in Manchuko with whom he had cohabited in Hongkong.

CONFIDENTIAL
POLICE HEADQUARTERS,
HONG KONG.
29th December, 1938.
Sir,
I have the honour to request your assistance
in tracing Mr. Robert George WITCHELL, a British subject,
30 years of age, who is employed as a clerk in the
Passport Office of this department. He left Hong Kong
for Shanghai on the 25th November, 1938, in the S.S.
"Empress of Asia" having been granted 12 days' casual
leave. He has not yet returned to duty, and although
he has already long over-stayed his leave I have re-
ceived no word of explanation from him.
I understand that Mr. Witchell's wife, Mrs.
M.K. Witchell, is living in Shanghai at No. 377 du
Roi Albert, Appartment 5. It is possible that she
may be able to give some information concerning her
husband although I understand that they have recently
not been on best of terms.
I shall be very grateful for any assistance
you can give me in this matter.
I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
（签名：Merdue）
Act. Commissioner of Police.
The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

CGP/AHT
机密
香港警察总部。
1938年12月29日。
先生，
谨请阁下协助查找罗伯特·乔治·威切尔（Robert George WITCHELL）先生，英籍，30岁，系本部门护照科职员。他于1938年11月25日获准12天事假，乘坐“亚细亚皇后”号轮船离开香港前往上海。他至今未返岗，尽管假期早已超期，但我未收到他的任何解释。
据悉，威切尔先生的妻子M.K. 威切尔太太（Mrs. M.K. Witchell）居住在上海阿尔贝特王路（du Roi Albert）377号5室。她或许能提供有关其丈夫的一些信息，尽管我了解到他们近期关系并不和睦。
如蒙阁下在此事上给予任何协助，不胜感激。
谨致
敬礼，
（签名：Merdue）
代理警务处处长。
致：
上海工部局警务处处长，
上海。
